newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson trial to resume after holiday break.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson trial to resume after holiday break.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's civil trial was due to resume on Monday with plaintiffs' attorneys grilling an expert witness who said a picture of the ex-football star wearing expensive Italian shoes was probably faked.

A source familiar with the plaintiffs' case told Reuters they would probably introduce a second picture showing Simpson wearing the Bruno Magli shoes identical to those which left a trail of bloody footprints leading from the murder scene where Simpson's ex-wife and her friend were killed.

Robert Groden, a photographic technician, testified for the defence last month before the two-week holiday break in the case that a photograph of Simpson taken in Buffalo during a Buffalo Bills game in 1993 had been doctored to show him wearing Bruno Maglis. That photograph, taken by a freelance photographer, appeared in the National Enquirer.
But recently a second photograph, taken during the same game by a different photographer and also showing Simpson wearing what appears to be Bruno Maglis, surfaced in a Buffalo Bills fan magazine.
"It is probable that this (second) photograph will also be introduced in evidence by the plaintiffs," the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said.
Legal analysts say that could prove to be a difficult problem for Simpson's defence team, who would then have to convince the jury that both photographs were doctored.

Simpson, who told lawyers in his deposition in the civil case he would never wear such "ugly" shoes as Bruno Maglis, was acquitted in October 1995, of the June 12, 1994, murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.
He is now battling a civil wrongful deaths lawsuit brought by the families of the victims who are seeking substantial financial damages.

According to a list supplied by Simpson's attorneys to the plaintiffs' lawyers, Groden will be followed by four Los Angeles Police Department officers who had marginal roles in the murder investigation, then Simpson's houseguest at the time, Brian "Kato" Kaelin, will take the witness stand for the second time in the civil case.

The defence intends to call another 19 witnesses before closing its case, according to the list supplied to the plaintiffs' attorneys. Among them are Dr. Henry Lee, a prominent forensic expert who testified for Simpson at his criminal trial, whose testimony this time around will be seen by the jury on videotape.

Simpson, who was earlier called by the plaintiffs' lawyers and spent two days testifiying, will be called to the stand by his defence lawyers as their second-to-last witness. His daughter, Arnelle, from his first marriage to Marquerite Simpson, will be the emotional last witness.
Simpson is expected to testify on Thursday followed by his daughter on Friday.

There will then be rebuttal witnesses called by both sides followed by closing arguments, with the jury expected to get the case for consideration by the end of the second week of January, according to the source.
